title: Tax myth vs fact: a write-off still costs you money
label: Tax myth vs fact

lines: Maya buys a $1,000 laptop for her business.
So the IRS pays for it?

beats.note: Self-employed: $220 income tax + $141 self-employment tax. Federal only.

beats.text: Buy it because the business *needs it.*

cta.sub: We'll DM you our Is It Deductible? tool.

captions.instagram:
"It's a write-off" doesn't mean it costs nothing.

✔️ A deduction lowers your taxable income, not your bill dollar for dollar.
✔️ Example: a self-employed owner in the 22% federal bracket spends $1,000 on a business laptop. Income tax drops about $220 and self-employment tax about $141 (15.3% on 92.35% of the amount).
✔️ That's about $361 back. The other $639 is still your money.
✔️ Spend because the business needs it, then make sure you claim it.

Not sure if something counts? Our Is It Deductible? tool checks 59 common expenses.
